History:
- Presenting complaint: 4 days of feeling "under the weather" — sore throat, runny nose, progressing to dry cough.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~4 days ago with sore throat and rhinorrhea.
  - Sore throat painful for 1–2 days, now improving.
  - Dry cough began ~1 day ago and is constant.
  - Initial fever early in course, now improved with paracetamol and ibuprofen.
  - Night sweats and generalized fatigue for the past 3–4 days.
  - New myalgias and intermittent, generalized headaches over the past couple of days.
  - Mild exertional dyspnea ("winded" with exercise) but no breathing difficulty at rest.
- Associated symptoms/negatives:
  - Nasal congestion/obstruction.
  - Painful swallowing initially; patient did not inspect throat and reports no noted white spots.
  - No ear pain or discharge.
  - No chest pain at rest.
  - No nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, photophobia, visual changes, or urinary symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: patient states "otherwise fit and well." No chronic medical problems reported.
- Medications: Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented; Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented. Patient reports no other regular medications.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Family history: Grandmother with type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather had eczema.
- Social history: Lives alone; works as an accountant. Occasional cigar smoking (social/company events). Occasional alcohol socially.

Physical Examination:
- Telemedicine visit; no objective vital signs or in-person exam documented.
- Patient-reported findings:
  - No throat swelling reported (patient did not examine throat visually).
  - No ear symptoms reported.
  - No chest pain at rest; shortness of breath only on exertion.
  - Alert and oriented; able to perform activities of daily living and attend work with reduced capacity.
- Relevant negatives from review of systems: no rash, no GI upset, no visual disturbances.

Impression:
- Suspected acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (viral URTI), possible early influenza — clinically consistent with 4-day history of sore throat, rhinorrhea, dry cough, myalgias, transient fever.

Management Plan:
- Symptomatic care advised:
  - Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen for fever/aches (doses not documented).
  - Rest, stay well-hydrated, consider taking 1–2 days off work.
- Safety-net / return precautions:
  - Return for earlier review if high fever persists, breathing becomes more labored, or chest pain develops.
  - If not improved by one week from presentation, arrange follow-up appointment.
- No tests, prescriptions, or immediate referrals documented during this consult.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 4 days of sore throat and rhinorrhea progressing to a persistent dry cough, with initial fever that improved on paracetamol/ibuprofen, plus fatigue, night sweats, myalgias, and exertional shortness of breath. Likely a self-limited viral URTI. Advised symptomatic care (rest, fluids, analgesics) and to return if worse or not improved in one week.

Key Takeaways:
- Rest, stay well-hydrated, and continue paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed.
- Take 1–2 days off work if possible to aid recovery.
- Seek earlier medical attention for high/persistent fever, worsening shortness of breath, or new chest pain.

Next Steps:
- No investigations or prescriptions ordered at this visit.
- Follow-up appointment if symptoms persist at 1 week.
- Immediate re-evaluation if fever worsens, breathing difficulty increases, or chest pain occurs.

- Missing but clinically expected elements: objective vital signs (temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO2), in-person throat/chest exam findings, throat inspection, COVID/Influenza testing status, influenza/COVID vaccination history, exact doses/routes/frequencies for paracetamol and ibuprofen, smoking quantity/pack-years.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality comment: audio generally clear with minimal interruptions; some brief pauses and filler words but clinical information adequately captured.
